mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its long-run average for at least three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which is associated with higher corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: In 20 days following the trigger, SPX 20-day return is negative and remains so for the next 60 days (cumulative loss > 5% from trigger).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) above 2% for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as firms anticipate higher future sales and invest accordingly.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns over the 60-day horizon are negative and statistically indistinguishable from a baseline of no change in HOUST (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% followed by a rebound of >3% in the subsequent month creates a supply-shock anticipation effect, producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -5.0 one month then INDPRO > 3.0 the next month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10) during the 20-day window after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be negative due to market anticipation of rate hikes and reduced equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns over the 60-day horizon are all positive and exceed the pre-inflation average by at least 5% (cumulative).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% without a corresponding increase in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and pushes S&P 500 forward returns to the positive over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 and PAYEMS does not increase by >5% in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market tightening without participation surge
failure_condition: SPX 20-day return is negative and remains so for the next 60-day window despite continued tight labor conditions (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail sales proxies (not available in evidence catalog; fallback to GDP demand proxies) are not applicable here. Instead, a sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by >4% for three months predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days due to market panic about demand collapse.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day return is not significantly different from zero (p > 0.10) during the 5-day window following the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer confidence proxies (not available; fallback to a supply shock via RSAFS: retail sales) when RSAFS increases by >8% in a month predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as markets anticipate inventory drawdowns and potential restocking cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day return is negative and statistically indistinguishable from baseline (p > 0.10) during the 20-day window after the trigger.
